newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says losing air force edge over India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says losing air force edge over India.

text.p: Pakistan is losing an air force edge over arch-foe India because of the high price of new comparable jets, Pakistan Air Force (PAF) chief Air Chief Marshal Abbas Khattak said on Wednesday.

He told reporters that the PAF had always been far behind the Indian Air Force in numerical strength but had maintained a qualitative edge, particularly after getting U.S.-made F-16 fighters in the 1980s.
"That qualitative edge which he had before 1992 is eroding," he said.
"After the acquisition of (French) Mirage-2000, (British) Jaguars and (Russian) MiG-29s by the Indian Air Force, we are now also losing the qualitative edge."

Khattak, answering reporters' questions after attending an inaugural session of Pakistan's new parliament along with other armed forces chiefs, said Pakistan wanted to buy French Mirage 2000-5s after the United States refused to sell more F-16s in 1990 but they were cost prohibitive.
"It is a very capable aircraft," he said. "Whether the country can afford it or not is for the government to decide."
Pakistani officials said last year the aircraft would cost $80 million to $90 million each compared to the original $23 million apiece price tag on F-16s.
"It has good missiles and a good system. But we don't have the money to buy it."
Khattak said the PAF was also looking for other options but added that Russia was not willing to sell SU-27 aircraft and no other "capable" aircraft were available to Islamabad at present.
He said Pakistan was spending double the amount on the maintenance of F-16s after Washington banned all military sales to Pakistan under the so-called Pressler Amendment law in 1990.
"Now we have to purchase the spares from the open market which are more expensive."
In May last year, Pakistan signed an agreement with France for buying used 40 Mirage III fighters for $120 million.
